titleEn: Going nuclear on livestock methane emissions
titleZh: IAEA与贝尔法斯特女王大学合作利用核技术减少牲畜甲烷排放
summaryZh: 联合国国际原子能机构与贝尔法斯特女王大学合作开展为期五年的研究项目，利用核技术工具识别与甲烷排放相关的动物性状，通过育种和营养干预提高牲畜生产力，从而降低单位产品的甲烷排放强度。项目聚焦瘤胃微生物组表型分析，旨在为全球政策提供依据，帮助农民在环保约束下维持盈利。
featuredReason: 该新闻揭示了国际权威机构将核技术应用于牲畜甲烷减排和育种的前沿动向，虽不直接涉及IoT/AI，但为智慧畜牧的精准育种和瘤胃微生物组监测提供了政策与科研风向标，值得关注行业减排技术路线的读者阅读。
contentFull: Top Stories Beef Dairy Sheep Tillage Machinery Northern Ireland Videos Podcasts Top Stories Beef Dairy Sheep Tillage Machinery Northern Ireland Videos Podcasts Going nuclear on livestock methane emissions ![Image 1: Elena Conroy Garcia By Elena Conroy Garcia October 17, 2026 12:00 PM](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsauthorelena-conroy-garcia) Share this article ![Image 2](https:www.agriland.iefarming-newsgoing-nuclear-on-livestock-methane-emissions) Reducing livestock methane emissions has become such a pressing issue for agriculture that the United Nations' International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is taking up the cause. And it is doing so in collaboration with Queen's University Belfast (QUB). The university is participating in a research project that aims to increase livestock productivity and identify the right animal traits for breeding programmes in order to reduce methane emissions. The coordinated research project will involve the IAEA and the use of nuclear tools, with the target of breeding stronger and healthier livestock. These animals will be able to produce more meat and milk and provide a steady food supply which will reduce the intensity of methane. According to the IAEA, methane emissions can serve as an indicator of metabolic efficiency. "Animals that produce more methane per unit of feed consumed generally have lower feed conversion efficiency," it said. The main aim of the research to advise countries on the use of nuclear tools to improve livestock breeding and strengthen food security have a direct knock-on effect on methane emissions. Farmers will be provided with go-to advice on best breeding practices for best dietary interventions and also on how to optimise productivity. Farming benefits Professor in animal science and microbiology, and QUB team lead for the project, Sharon Huws, spoke to Agriland about the benefits this research will have to farm productivity. According to Prof. Huws, the research will feed into global policies that will make ultimately make farming more profitable while remaining environmentally conscious. She highlighted the pressures agricultural communities are facing in terms of population growth, rising demand for animal-source foods, and climate change. Prof Huws said: “Agriculture is at the centre of communities and it always has been. "We have a major pressure really to make sure that we are as sustainable as we can be. “We're seeing the smaller farms no longer being farmed or being sold because they can't maintain an income if you have to reduce your animal numbers because of environmental constraints.” This research, which aims to improve animal health and breed livestock with optimal features will “ultimately put pounds in pockets,” according to the professor. “And because that means that, then per kilogram of milk or meat produced, you're reducing the intensity of methane when it's expressed as product produced," she said. Methane Huws outlines that targeting methane without any incentives in place creates massive issues for farmers as they do not benefit from them at all. She said: “It's a major global challenge and there are numerous policies across the world, you know, requiring us to reduce methane from animals. “Governments are on for carbon credit schemes and things of that nature, but ultimately, no farmer will put anything in place that isn't viable for the business. "This why this research is so important for the future of farming; if farmers can ensure productive and health livestock then they can reduce herd numbers." Research Queen’s is tasked with providing expert guidance on 'Nutritional and Rumen Microbiome-Based Phenotyping of Livestock Productivity and Methane Mitigation Traits', throughout the five-year project. The aim is to advise farmers on best breeding practices for ruminants, best dietary interventions and also on how to optimise rumen microbiome for productivity. The QUB team will be led by Prof. Huws and co-led by Dr. Katerina Theodoridou. They will work alongside Dr. Kayley Barnes from the Institute for Global Food Security and School of Biological Sciences at QUB. Dr. Barnes said: “Queen’s will provide expertise on the differences between microbial communities in the rumen, which is the largest and first compartment of the stomach in cud-chewing animals.” translationZh:
减少牲畜甲烷排放已成为农业面临的紧迫问题，以至于联合国国际原子能机构（IAEA）正在着手推动这一事业。该机构正与贝尔法斯特女王大学（QUB）合作开展此项工作。

该大学正在参与一个研究项目，旨在提高牲畜生产力并确定适合育种计划的正确动物性状，以减少甲烷排放。这项协调研究项目将涉及IAEA和核工具的使用，目标是培育更强壮、更健康的牲畜。这些动物将能够生产更多的肉和奶，并提供稳定的食物供应，从而降低甲烷排放强度。

据IAEA称，甲烷排放可以作为代谢效率的指标。该机构表示：“每单位饲料消耗产生更多甲烷的动物，通常饲料转化效率较低。”

该研究的主要目标是向各国提供关于使用核工具改善牲畜育种和加强粮食安全的建议，这些建议对甲烷排放有直接的连锁效应。农民将获得关于最佳育种实践、最佳饮食干预以及如何优化生产力的实用建议。

**农业效益**

动物科学与微生物学教授、QUB项目团队负责人Sharon Huws向Agriland讲述了这项研究将给农场生产力带来的好处。

Huws教授表示，这项研究将为全球政策提供依据，最终使农业在保持环保意识的同时更加有利可图。她强调了农业社区在人口增长、对动物源食品需求上升以及气候变化方面面临的压力。

Huws教授说：“农业一直处于社区的中心，历来如此。我们确实面临着确保尽可能可持续发展的巨大压力。我们看到小型农场不再被耕种或被出售，因为如果由于环境限制而不得不减少动物数量，它们就无法维持收入。”

这项旨在改善动物健康并培育具有最佳特征的牲畜的研究，“最终将把钱放进口袋”，这位教授说。“因为这意味着，每生产一公斤牛奶或肉，当以产品产量来表达时，你正在降低甲烷的强度，”她说。

**甲烷**

Huws指出，在没有激励措施的情况下针对甲烷采取措施会给农民带来巨大问题，因为他们根本无法从中受益。她说：“这是一个重大的全球性挑战，世界各地有许多政策要求我们减少动物的甲烷排放。各国政府正在推行碳信用计划之类的东西，但最终，没有农民会实施对生意不可行的措施。这就是为什么这项研究对农业的未来如此重要；如果农民能够确保牲畜高产健康，他们就可以减少畜群数量。”

**研究**

在为期五年的项目中，女王大学负责提供关于“牲畜生产力与甲烷减排性状的营养和瘤胃微生物组表型分析”的专家指导。目标是就反刍动物的最佳育种实践、最佳饮食干预以及如何优化瘤胃微生物组以提高生产力向农民提供建议。

QUB团队将由Huws教授领导，Katerina Theodoridou博士共同领导。他们将与QUB全球粮食安全研究所和生物科学学院的Kayley Barnes博士合作。Barnes博士说：“女王大学将提供关于瘤胃微生物群落差异的专业知识，瘤胃是反刍动物胃中最大且第一个隔室。”
